premises.text: People want home security but traditional systems are hard to install, non-portable for renters, overreactive, and decor-unfriendly, so adoption stays under 20%
premises.evidence_span: the solutions that are available today are both broken and outdated

premises.text: Sentry is an all-in-one self-install hub with camera, motion, environmental sensors, mobile app, customizable themes, and control of Nest/Hue/Wemo devices
premises.evidence_span: an all-in-one solution to know and control your home from one single destination

premises.text: Primary early segments are urban dwellers and pet parents who need portable security
premises.evidence_span: the urban dweller market as well as pet parents

premises.text: Hardware-as-platform business: unit plus cloud video/media services and Android developer apps, offered around $299
premises.evidence_span: our business is really one of hardware as a platform

value.text: Modern households protect what matters with simple, elegant, portable home awareness and control

causal_links.evidence_span: while the majority of Americans, including myself, want to have home security, less than 20% of us actually do
self-installation process that takes minutes versus hours of expert installation
being able to take this solution on to go with them

notes: Install friction, non-portability, false alerts, and aesthetics folded as one broken-security problem (§4.1.6). Sensors, app, themes, smart-home integrations, and touchscreen roadmap folded as Sentry feature cascade (§4.1.7). Kickstarter $400k treated as traction. Anti-template: problem, hub product, and segment/platform packaging separately revisable.
